extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and institutional grant administrators (PD/PIs, AORs, research administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and requirements governing preparation, submission, post-submission materials, and administrative/ethical expectations for NIH grant applications and awards. Covers formatting, allowable supplemental materials, registrations, data-sharing, personnel documentation, submission limits, and reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted post-submission materials (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other post-submission materials specified in the NOFO for which the application was submitted or in a special Guide Notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may submit only materials explicitly allowed by the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) or special Guide Notice. Most other additions are not accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: News of an article accepted for publication (content limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: News of an article accepted for publication since submission of the application, which must include only: list of authors and institutional affiliations; title of the article; journal or citation (if available).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of articles, links to articles, or any other materials related to an article accepted for publication will not be accepted as post-submission materials, unless specified in the NOFO or a special Guide Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data as post-submission material (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will accept preliminary data as post-submission material for Type 1 R01, R21, or R03 applications, including resubmissions, if the NOFO used for submission allows preliminary data in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only permitted when the NOFO explicitly allows preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training grant additional post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: For Institutional Training and Training-related Grants (e.g., T32, T34, T35, T90, TU2, T15, D43, K12, KM1, UR2): news—since the training grant application was submitted—of a trainee's or former trainee's graduation, employment, promotion, funding, or publications; a faculty member's promotion, funding, or publications; and the addition or removal of any faculty member who will be involved in the training program (mentors or senior/key persons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of publications for Training Grants are allowed. Follow the page limits in the NIH Table of Page Limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship and career development application post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual Fellowship (F-Series) and Individual Career Development Award (K-series) applications may include: new information on the Sponsor/Mentor funding, limited to the project title, funding source (e.g., NIH grant number), a brief description of specific aims, and relevance to the fellowship or career development application under review; news of change in Mentor(s) or other Senior/Key Persons specified in the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference grant post-submission materials (R13, U13)
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-page explanation of all speakers who accepted invitations to participate in the proposed conference after the application was submitted, plus a one-page explanation of all speakers who declined such invitations after the application was submitted. Alternatively, a one-page explanation for each plenary slot on the agenda may be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limits for post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-submission materials must conform to NIH policies on font size, margins, and paper size referenced in the applicable application instructions. Any specified formats (e.g., budgets, biographical sketches) and page limits referenced in the applicable application instructions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If post-submission material is not required on a specific format page and does not have a specified page limit, each explanation or letter is limited to one page. If the application has multiple components, each subproject or core is allowed explanations or letters, but each is limited to one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission materials must be received by the NIH Scientific Review Officer (SRO) no later than 30 calendar days prior to the peer review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials will not be accepted if fewer than 30 calendar days remain before the peer review meeting, unless specifically stated otherwise in the NOFO or special Guide Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) concurrence for post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) of the applicant organization is required for submission of post-submission materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AOR must send materials directly to the SRO or send concurrence to the PD/PI who will forward materials and concurrence to the SRO. A communication from the PD/PI only or with a copy to the AOR will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials file type (PDF) and SRO upload
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission materials can only be submitted as a PDF attachment, except for video submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO is responsible for uploading acceptable materials into the official electronic grant file maintained in the eRA Commons; PD/PIs can check 'Additions for Review' to confirm upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable video content (non-traditional materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only acceptable content for videos is demonstrations of devices and experimental data with a temporal element (show how something functions or occurs over time) or demonstrates movement or change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: unusual interventions or surgical procedures, prototype model use, visualization of 3‑D structures or structural changes in molecules or cells, temporal changes in cell migration or interactions, demonstrations of interventions on animal behavior or kinetic physiopathology, software/database/mobile app demonstrations, educational materials or video games. No demonstrations of data that could be feasibly presented in figures or tables will be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable video content
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of unacceptable content include virtual tours of laboratories, equipment in place, platform presentations, testimonials, advertisements, or commercials, research or outreach presentations (unless requested by the SRO in lieu of a site visit).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application requirements when submitting videos
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be structured at submission to indicate that a video will be submitted subsequently. Key images/'stills' and a brief description of each video must be included within the page limits of the research strategy. A cover letter including intent to submit a video should also be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient descriptive information must be provided in the research strategy because not all reviewers may be able to access the video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video length, file-size, and format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple videos may be submitted per application but aggregate length must not exceed 2 minutes for single-project applications and 5 minutes for multi-component applications. Maximum file size for all videos combined is 35 MB. Acceptable digital formats are WMV, AVI, MOV, and MP4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Closed captioning is recommended. Digital files should not be embedded in another file format (e.g., PDF).

rubrics_metrics.name: Video submission procedure and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission video files should be sent via email as a digital file for upload to the application grant folder by the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with all post-submission materials, videos must be received by the SRO one month (30 calendar days) prior to the peer review meeting. AOR concurrence is required; videos containing unacceptable content or exceeding time/size limits will not be accepted. Applications with hyperlinks to videos or videos embedded in the research strategy may be considered in violation of page limits and may be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM registration and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicant organizations must register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and maintain a current and active registration at all times during which such organizations have an application under consideration for funding by NIH and, if an award is made, until final financial report or final payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A UEI is issued as part of SAM.gov registration and must be provided on application forms; the same UEI must be used for all registrations and on the grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate student compensation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The maximum amount NIH will award for support of a graduate student on a research grant is tied to the NRSA zero-level postdoctoral stipend in effect at the time the grant award is issued. Compensation includes salary or wages, fringe benefits, and tuition remission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compensation must be reasonable and consistent with institutional cost principles. NIH staff will review requested compensation for reasonableness; NIH will not request or accept modular budget revisions solely to review graduate compensation. Graduate compensation generally will not be considered reasonable if in excess of the amount paid to a first‑year postdoctoral scientist at the same institution performing comparable work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing (DMS) and Genomic Data Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant projects that generate scientific data are subject to the NIH Data Management and Sharing (DMS) policy. If applicable, genomic data sharing considerations must be submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section 8.2.3.1 Policy for Data Management and Sharing (DMS Policy) for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Fetal Tissue (HFT) funding restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 22, 2026, NIH funds are not permitted for research using Human Fetal Tissue from elective abortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ongoing projects as of that date, organizations may rebudget released funds to support research under the same project that is not unallowable under this policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch submission requirement and format conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires submission of a biographical sketch for each proposed senior/key personnel and other significant contributor for competing applications, progress reports when new senior/key personnel are identified, and to support prior approval requests for changes in senior/key personnel status and recipient organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications containing biosketches that do not conform to the required format may be withdrawn. See the NIH Biosketch page for format pages, instructions and the NIH disclosure table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission limits per PI
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will only accept six new, renewal, resubmission, or revision applications from an individual Principal Investigator/Program Director or Multiple Principal Investigator for all council rounds in a calendar year beginning with applications submitted for the September 25, 2025 due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: T (Training grants), R25 (Research Education Grants) and R13 (Conference Grants). This policy applies to all activity codes except listed exceptions; see FAQs for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in applications
rubrics_metrics.description: While NIH recognizes that AI tools may be appropriate to assist in limited aspects of application preparation, NIH will not consider applications that are either substantially developed by AI, or contain sections substantially developed by AI, to be original ideas of applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI use carries risks (e.g., plagiarism, research misconduct). If NIH identifies evidence of plagiarism, fabrication, or falsification, NIH will refer the matter to the HHS Office of Research Integrity for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application forms and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibit 3 lists required application forms for competing applications which vary by support mechanism (e.g., SF424 (R&R), PHS 398, PHS 416-1). These forms and associated instructions are available on the NIH Forms and Format Pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SF424 (R&R) form set, combined with PHS components, is used for electronic submission. Questions about forms may be directed to DGSI/OPERA, OER, NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic submission requirements and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires electronic submission of all competing (Type 1, Type 2) and administrative supplement (Type 3) applications; all RPPRs; and certain change of recipient organization and successor-in-interest applications. All applications must be successfully submitted electronically to Grants.gov on or before 5:00 p.m. local time on the appropriate date listed in the funding opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If due date falls on a weekend, it is extended to the following Monday; if on a Federal holiday, extended to the following business day. Timeliness is determined against the adjusted business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late application window and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a two-week window of consideration after the application due date during which NIH might consider accepting a late application. Acceptance of late applications will be made on a case-by-case basis dependent upon the explanation provided in a cover letter submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the Division of Receipt and Referral (DRR), Center for Scientific Review (CSR) has authority to accept a late application. Contacting DRR in advance will not influence acceptance. When due date extended due to weekend/holiday, the two-week window is calculated from the business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable circumstances for late applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not consider accepting late applications under certain circumstances, including: submissions to RFAs that declared 'No late applications will be accepted' and submissions to any NOFOs after the two-week window.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for late submission must relate to the individual(s) with the PD/PI role. For MPI applications, reasons may apply to any or all PD/PIs. This accommodation does not apply to co-Investigators, project leaders, or other Key Persons unless they also have MPI status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous Submission eligibility for NIH Federal Advisory Committee members
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous Submission allows eligible members of NIH Federal Advisory Committees to submit applications for certain grant activity codes after the standard due date, until the last day of the receipt period for each Advisory Council Round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligible categories include chartered NIH IRGs, Boards of Scientific Counselors, Advisory Boards or Councils, and Program Advisory Committees. Eligibility begins on appointment active date and continues for six weeks after official retirement date. Eligibility is visible in eRA Commons; admin roles can check eligibility via Admin module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on similar, essentially identical, or identical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous submissions of identical applications to one or more components of the PHS are not allowed, and NIH will not accept similar grant applications with essentially the same research focus from the same applicant organization for the same receipt date. Identical or essentially identical applications submitted by different applicant organizations will not be accepted for the same receipt date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may be delayed or not reviewed if reviewers identify multiple applications for essentially the same project. Exceptions: 1) individuals submitting an application for a K02 proposing essentially identical research in an application for an individual research project; 2) individuals submitting an individual research project identical to a subproject that is part of a program project or center grant application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application non-conformity consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-conformity with application requirements can have serious consequences; NIH may withdraw any application identified during receipt, referral and review that does not conform with the SF424 (R&R) Application Guide, the NOFO, and relevant Guide Notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: biosketches not in required format, nonconforming page limits, applications submitted as new containing elements of resubmission/renewal contrary to policy, submissions after 5 PM local time. If withdrawn, a letter will be placed in the eRA Commons Status page.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH response to natural disasters and emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For major disasters impacting many organizations, NIH will coordinate with other HHS components and Federal agencies to develop any additional response, considering federal disaster declarations, severity of damage, length of closure, impact on investigators and subjects, and community impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late applications due to natural disasters are subject to the late application policy. Specific NIH responses will be issued in NIH Guide Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud, waste, and abuse reporting obligations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals aware of fraud, waste, or abuse related to NIH grants should consider contacting their institution’s sponsored research/compliance office, the NIH CGMO listed in the NoA, the DGCO/OPERA/OER, or the HHS OIG Hotline. Allegations of non-criminal misuse and recipient conflict of interest should be reported to NIH OMA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include embezzlement, misuse/misappropriation of grant funds/property, false statements, charging ghost individuals, inflated rental fees, false financial reports. Federal government may pursue administrative, civil, or criminal action under statutes (e.g., Program Fraud Civil Remedies Act, Criminal False Claims Act, Civil False Claims Act). NIH may administratively recover misspent funds pursuant to 2 CFR Part 200.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of grant-related information (public access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for certain proprietary or private information, most grant-related information submitted to NIH is considered public information and, once an award is made, is subject to possible release to individuals or organizations outside NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH routinely posts awarded grant information (project title, PD/PI name, project description) on RePORT and sends project descriptions to NTIS. Several policies require acknowledgment of support and disclaimers for publications, inventions, and other research products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and identification of proprietary information
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are discouraged from submitting proprietary information unless essential for evaluation. If the application contains trade secrets, commercial/financial, privileged, or confidential information, the pages containing that information should be identified as specified in the application instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such information is furnished to the Federal government in confidence for evaluation; NIH will protect it from unauthorized disclosure consistent with peer review confidentiality and FOIA/Privacy Act requirements. If a grant is awarded, the Federal government has the right to use or disclose the information to the extent authorized by law; this does not limit government use if information is obtained without restriction from another source.
